svg.text: Carrier 24ABB3 — how it’s wired
A beginner-friendly map of the real parts and how the wires connect them. The real manual is one tap away.
HIGH VOLTAGE · 240V
— the power that actually runs the compressor & fan
LOW VOLTAGE · 24V
— the small signal from inside that switches it on

g.text: the switch that powers the unit on

svg.text: WHAT EACH WIRE DOES
match a wire’s number on the drawing · ● = wires joined
One leg of the 240-volt power to the contactor.
Second leg of the 240-volt power to the contactor.
Contactor load leg powers the compressor common.
Contactor load leg powers the compressor run terminal.
Compressor start winding to the run-capacitor terminal.
Run-capacitor common tied to compressor run terminal.
Run-capacitor fan terminal powers the outdoor fan motor.
Outdoor fan motor return to the contactor load leg.
24-volt path from contactor coil to low-pressure safety…
Low-pressure switch in series to discharge-temp switch.
Discharge-temp switch in series to high-pressure switch.
High-pressure switch to the compressor time-delay input.
Time-delay output energizes the contactor coil.
24-volt hot from the transformer to the time-delay.
Liquid-line solenoid tied into the safety string.
Liquid-line solenoid return toward transformer common.
WHAT THE LETTERS MEAN
L1 / L2
the two 240-volt power legs in
T1 / T2
power leaving the contactor
C · R · S
compressor: Common / Run / Start
HERM
capacitor → compressor (“hermetic”)
FAN
capacitor → the fan motor
LPS · HPS
low / high-pressure safety switch
DTS · CTD
discharge-temp switch · time-delay
“C” = Common everywhere — but a different wire each place.
